title: BOAC 781
summary: BOAC Flight 781, a de Havilland Comet operating from Singapore to London, suffered explosive decompression while at altitude over the Mediterranean Sea near Elba on January 10, 1954. The pressurized cabin ruptured catastrophically, causing the aircraft to break up in mid-air. All 35 aboard were killed. Post-crash investigation identified metal fatigue cracks initiating from design stress concentration points around the cabin windows and fuselage-to-wing junction. This accident led to major changes in aircraft design standards and inspection practices worldwide.
probable_cause: Structural failure of the pressure cabin resulting from fatigue cracks initiated at stress concentration points around cabin window corners and fuselage design joints, leading to explosive decompression and in-flight breakup.

factors.evidence: Fatigue cracks developed in cabin roof and structural joints
Design stress concentration points around windows lacked adequate fatigue strength
Pressure cabin failed at the fatigue crack initiation point
Cabin pressurization was suddenly lost, rupturing lungs of occupants
Debris caught fire after impact with sea
